task: Layer-2 stability measurement (14 cases x 5 reps x 2 conditions)

failures.what: First full run (340 calls attempted over 20 min) failed 100% with HTTPError: key() in l2_p0_3_eval.py fell back to UTIM_NVIDIA_KEY (nvapi-... NVIDIA key) and sent it to api.vultrinference.com -> 422 'Invalid API key'. Error handler recorded only exception type, discarding the HTTP status/body. No preflight existed, so ~250 garbage ERROR rows accumulated before the shell timeout killed the run.
failures.root_cause: Key-resolution fallback picked a provider-mismatched key; no preflight validation of key+endpoint before batch; error capture dropped status code making diagnosis blind.
failures.what_i_did_wrong: Trusted P0-3's implicit key resolution without verifying which key would be used against which endpoint; ran a 340-call batch with no smoke test; error path lost diagnostic detail.
failures.fix: Added preflight() single-call gate (aborts on http>=400 before any batch work), explicit 4xx fail-fast with status+body capture in call_one, and ran with VULTR_SI_API_KEY explicitly set (verified http 200 first).

failures.what: Harness loaded all 34 cases (including 20 controls) instead of the authorized 14-case series (6 premise + 8 scope); first run would have measured 340 observations instead of 140.
failures.root_cause: No group filter and no count assertion against the authorization scope.
failures.what_i_did_wrong: Translated 'same 14-case series' into 'load the cases file' without filtering to the specified groups; authorization scope not encoded as an assertion.
failures.fix: Filter SERIES_GROUPS=('premise','scope') + assert len(cases)==14; deleted stale records so resume started clean.

failures.what: After the successful 140-call run, analyze() crashed with TypeError ('int' object is not iterable) on the cost calculation — a sum() misuse in a generator expression.
failures.root_cause: cost = (sum(t) * USD_PER_M_IN / 1e6 for t in tin) built a generator of floats but the next line called sum(cost) where cost was... actually the generator expression `sum(t)*rate for t in tin` — the bug: parenthesized generator assigned, then sum(cost) summed correctly, but the inner expression `sum(t)` treated each token count t as an iterable. Typo: meant `t * rate`.
failures.what_i_did_wrong: Wrote the cost generator without a syntax/dry-run check on the analysis path; the run itself (140 calls, ~$0.10, 9.3 min) was already complete and safe on disk, but the report was not produced on first try.
failures.fix: Corrected to sum(t * RATE / 1e6 ...); re-ran in resume mode (0 new API calls); added independent recomputation script (l2_stability_verify.py) that re-derives every headline metric from the raw JSONL via a separate code path.

impact: Wasted one 20-minute shell window and ~250 invalid API attempts (all rejected at http 422 before inference — no model cost). No experiment data lost; the authorized 140-call measurement completed cleanly after fixes. Cost of the real measurement: $0.10245.
systemic_note: Batch LLM harnesses in this project must (a) preflight key+endpoint, (b) assert authorization scope counts, (c) capture HTTP status+body in errors. P0-3's harness shared defects (a) and (c) but got lucky with the key.
